title: Transfer of compactness to the pro-étale localizing category
statement:
Fix the standing finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and a finite commutative ring $A$ with $\ell^rA=0$ for some $r\ge0$. Give $A$ the discrete topology. Use the unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ of module objects over the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring $A_X$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\Dctf(X,A)$ be its full subcategory of bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and let $\mathcal L=\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$ be the full replete triangulated, small-coproduct-closed hull with ambient coproducts [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Then every $C\in\Dctf(X,A)$ is compact in $\mathcal L$: for every small family $(K_s)_{s\in S}$ of objects of $\mathcal L$, the canonical map
$$\bigoplus_{s\in S}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal L}(C,K_s)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal L}\!\left(C,\bigoplus_{s\in S}K_s\right)$$
is bijective [def-pc-compact-object], with smallness relative to [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Identify finite coefficients before using the ordinary comparison theorems. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] with $B=A$, and then [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] with $T=X$. They identify the pulled-back condensed ring $A_X$ with the constant $A$-ring sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Write $\theta:A_{\mathrm{const}}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$ for this ring isomorphism. An $A_X$-action $\gamma:A_X\otimes M\to M$ becomes the constant-ring action $\gamma\circ(\theta\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$; an action $\delta$ over the constant ring becomes $\delta\circ(\theta^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$. The two resulting functors are inverse and leave underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged; therefore they preserve exact sequences and coproducts. Applied degreewise, they identify the unbounded derived categories and their ambient coproducts. The same transport identifies tensor products by their bilinear universal property, hence derived tensor products, and identifies finite constant local models. Thus constructibility and finite Tor amplitude in the item agree with the ordinary constant-$A$ conventions in [det-ctf-finite-comparison-localizing]. On the étale side use the ordinary category of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

source.place: Opening paragraph: coefficient conventions for the two comparison functors

proof.text: Check the hypotheses of finite-Tor comparison. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $X$ has a finite affine cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with each $B_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], each $U_i$ has descending chain condition on closed subsets, equivalently ascending chain condition on opens. An increasing sequence of opens of $X$ stabilizes on each of the finitely many $U_i$ and thus on $X$. Every open $V\subseteq X$ is quasi-compact: finite unions from any open covering of $V$ have a maximal member by this ascending chain condition; that member contains every covering open. In particular $X$ is quasi-compact, and the inverse image under its diagonal of any affine open of $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ is an open of $X$ and hence quasi-compact. This is quasi-separatedness by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Also $A$ is Noetherian because each ideal is the finite set of its elements and these elements generate it [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. These arguments include the empty scheme and zero ring. The standing field is algebraically closed and $\ell$ is invertible in it.

source.place: Opening paragraph: qcqs and finite Noetherian hypotheses of the finite-Tor comparison

proof.text: Write $F=\nu_X^*$ for the comparison pullback. With the ordinary coefficient categories identified in step 1, [lem-sfb-unbounded-site-comparison] applies: $X$ is finite type over the algebraically closed field $k$, $\ell$ is invertible, and $A$ is finite commutative and killed by a power of $\ell$. Thus $F$ is exact, fully faithful and preserves all small coproducts on the unbounded categories. Apply [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] with $\Lambda=A$, using the qcqs and Noetherian checks in step 2. Its equivalence gives an object $C_0\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ and an isomorphism $c:FC_0\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. The source category $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ of [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] uses constructibility in the sense of [def-pe-etale-constructible-module] (a finite constructible partition of each affine open, finitely generated local models), whereas [det-ctf-finite-compact-etale] uses the global convention of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] (one finite constructible stratification of $X$, finite local models). They agree here. Since $A$ is finite, finitely generated $A$-modules are exactly the finite ones. If a sheaf $\mathcal F$ is constructible in the first sense, take the finite affine cover $U_1,\dots,U_n$ of step 2 and the partitions $U_i=\coprod_aZ_{ia}$, and put $W_i=U_i\setminus(U_1\cup\dots\cup U_{i-1})$. The sets $W_i\cap Z_{ia}$ are pairwise disjoint, cover $X$ and are locally closed in $X$. Hence they are constructible, because $X$ is a Noetherian space by step 2 [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Give them the reduced induced structure; the immersion into $X$ then factors through $Z_{ia}$, so the inverse image of $\mathcal F$ is a pullback of the finite locally constant sheaf $\mathcal F|_{Z_{ia}}$, which is again finite locally constant after pulling back its étale cover. Conversely, a global stratification meets each affine open $U$ in locally closed, hence constructible, subsets of the Noetherian space $U$, with the same local models. So the two bounded constructible subcategories coincide. The Tor-amplitude condition stated in [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] uses the same derived tensor against every module sheaf in degree zero as [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Hence $C_0$ lies in the $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ of [det-ctf-finite-compact-etale]. With a single finite Tor interval, [det-ctf-finite-compact-etale], for the same standing $k,X,\ell,A$ and ordinary étale category, makes $C_0$ compact against every object of $D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$.

source.place: First paragraph, and compactness input in the displayed Hom calculation

proof.text: For a small family $(K_s)_{s\in S}$ in $\mathcal L$, apply the first conclusion of [det-ctf-finite-comparison-localizing], for exactly the standing hypotheses and coefficient conventions checked above. It gives an exact coproduct-preserving equivalence from $\Loc(\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A))$ onto $\mathcal L$. Choose étale objects $M_s$ in the source closure and isomorphisms $a_s:FM_s\xrightarrow{\sim}K_s$. Only this equivalence clause is used; no compatibility with operations is needed. In particular the $M_s$ are ordinary unbounded étale objects, so compactness of $C_0$ applies to this entire family. By [sk-def-localizing-closure], $\bigoplus_sK_s$ is its ambient coproduct and lies in $\mathcal L$. Coproduct preservation from step 3 identifies it with $F(\bigoplus_sM_s)$ by the isomorphism $a:F(\bigoplus_sM_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_sK_s$ characterized by $a\circ F(\iota_s^{\mathrm{ét}})=\iota_s\circ a_s$ for every $s$.

source.place: Second paragraph: every localizing object has an étale antecedent, and sums are ambient

proof.text: Full faithfulness and the chosen isomorphisms give bijections $u\mapsto a_sF(u)c^{-1}$ from $\operatorname{Hom}(C_0,M_s)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(C,K_s)$, and $v\mapsto aF(v)c^{-1}$ from $\operatorname{Hom}(C_0,\bigoplus_sM_s)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(C,\bigoplus_sK_s)$. Under these bijections, the étale compactness map is the asserted pro-étale map: for each summand, $aF(\iota_su)c^{-1}=\iota_sa_sF(u)c^{-1}$ by the defining component of $a$, and additivity gives this identity for each finite-support sum. The étale compactness map is bijective by [det-ctf-finite-compact-etale], so the pro-étale one is bijective. Fullness of $\mathcal L$ and its ambient coproducts [sk-def-localizing-closure] make these exactly its Hom groups and compactness map, proving compactness as defined in [def-pc-compact-object]. The empty family gives $0\to\operatorname{Hom}(C,0)=0$; $C=0$, $A=0$ or $X=\varnothing$ also gives zero groups, so no exception is needed.
